evidence.excerpt:
Self-supervised learning in Vision Transformer models, such as DINO, enables
robust visual perception without requiring labeled data by leveraging large-scale
image datasets. However, these models lack a focusing mechanism during training,
resulting in perceptual representations that are often ambiguous or overly similar.
In this work, we introduce two visual focusing loss functions designed to establish
correspondence between the model's attention and specific regions within images.
Specifically, we leverage the multi-head attention mechanism within the model to
selectively steer the model's focus, leading to the emergence of spatial attention
head specialization, characterized by diverse and spatially focused perceptual capa-
bilities without requiring annotations. Through both qualitative and quantitative
evaluations, we demonstrate that our method substantially increases the

We consider self-supervised learning settings, such as DINO (Caron et al., 2021), where teacher and
student models are used and training is performed by minimizing a loss function between the two
models. To enable the model to acquire the ability to focus on the ROI, we propose to introduce two
visual focusing loss functions as shown in Fig. 2.
First, we briefly introduce the PHS method (Nozawa et al., 2025) for modifying the model's output
using the ROI. Once the ROIR is specified, the attention heads that produce the largest outputs of
attention maps within the ROI are selected. By applying the head selection method (Gong et al., 2021;
Meng et al., 2022; Ni et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2022; Nicolicioiu et al., 2023; Basile et al., 2025) that em-
phasizes the outputs of the selected heads, the model's overall output is modified to align with theROI.

To validate the ability of ViT models to focus on various regions within images, we evaluate their
zero-shot image segmentation performance. We follow a standard protocol (Chefer et al., 2021)
for evaluating the effectiveness of their heat maps. For each heat map, we compute the head mean
of the attention maps, where we use the [CLS] tokens from each head in the last attention layer
as the attention maps. We then binarize the heat map into a foreground/background segmentation
map, where the patch mean of the heat map is used for the threshold value. We utilize two datasets,
ImageNet-Segmentation (Guillaumin et al., 2014) and PASCAL VOC (Everingham et al., 2010), for
the evaluation following Chefer et al. (2021) and Helbling et al. (2025). ImageNet-Segmentation

evidence.excerpt:
A Limitations
While our method can train the model to focus on diverse regions within an image, it does not
allow explicit control over where each attention head focuses, as the regions of focus are determined
implicitly during training. As a result, it is not possible to know in advance which regions each
attention head will focus on until after training. Our method also increases the training time and
introduces a trade-off between classification performance and performance improvements in zero-shot
segmentation, object discovery, and FOIR tasks. Exploring other effective ways to utilize the visual
focusing image representations obtained by our method remains an important direction for future
work.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on external human-annotated datasets (ImageNet-Segmentation, PASCAL VOC, MS-COCO, ADE20k, Cityscapes) using standardized protocols not used during self-supervised pretraining.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark ground-truth object annotations across mIoU, Acc, and mAP for zero-shot segmentation, CorLoc for object discovery, and mIoU for supervised semantic segmentation.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Self-distillation cross-entropy losses between student and teacher representations, where the student output is modified by prompt-guided attention head selection using randomly sampled crop and mask boxes without ground-truth semantic annotations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The empirical findings support the claimed trade-offs and improvements, showing consistent gains in dense zero-shot localization and spatial diversity alongside an acknowledged slight reduction in single-label global classification accuracy.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation thoroughly tests the claimed emergent spatial specialization across multiple independent standard benchmarks, including zero-shot segmentation (ImageNet-Seg, PASCAL VOC), unsupervised object discovery (LOST on VOC07, VOC12, COCO), image retrieval, and supervised semantic segmentation (ADE20k, Cityscapes, VOC). Ablations on loss weights, head selection counts, entropy metrics, and continual learning validate the mechanism.

evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark ground-truth object annotations across mIoU, Acc, and mAP for zero-shot segmentation, CorLoc for object discovery, and mIoU for supervised semantic segmentation.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Self-distillation cross-entropy losses between student and teacher representations incorporating crop- and mask-based visual prompt head selection without ground-truth semantic annotations.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report the lack of explicit deterministic control over which head attends where, increased training overhead, and the slight degradation in k-NN and linear classification performance on ImageNet.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is explicitly defined, modifying self-distillation (DINOv2) by pairing cropped and masked teacher views with prompt-guided head-selected student outputs. Full training hyperparameters, architecture variations (ViT-B, ViT-L, ViT-g with registers), ablation settings, and loss formulations are clearly documented.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides clear methodological definitions, extensive empirical evaluations across diverse tasks and model sizes, and rigorous baselines with honest reporting of trade-offs, satisfying quality standards.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces two visual focusing loss functions (inside-focus and outside-focus) based on prompt-guided attention head selection for self-supervised Vision Transformers to encourage spatial attention head specialization and improve dense visual representation tasks without human annotations.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides clear methodological definitions, extensive empirical evaluations across diverse tasks and model sizes, and rigorous baselines with honest reporting of trade-offs, satisfying quality standards.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report the lack of explicit deterministic control over which head attends where, increased training overhead, and the slight degradation in k-NN and linear classification performance on ImageNet.
